name: Salt flat
notes: Bare salt crust in the centre with a thin ring of succulent halophytes (glasswort, iodine bush, seepweed) and saltgrass at the margins, greasewood and tamarisk on the outer rim; Bonneville/Death Valley playas, Saharan chotts, Central Asian sabkhas, Salar de Uyuni.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny hair-tufted seeds sprout within a day on wet silt; the seedling has two minute cotyledons and thread-thin, jointed grey-green shoots. It soon makes a single fast leader clothed in drooping, apparently leafless jointed twigs (leaves reduced to tiny sheaths), like a young she-oak, then a broad, dense evergreen tree; it also suckers from roots.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tamarix aphylla (tree to 18 m; spreads by seed, suckers and cuttings); ICRAF Agroforestree (to 18 m, 60-80 cm dbh, roots ~10 m deep; fuelwood cut from the 4th year after planting); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (germination <24 h, seed viable only weeks). Height-age curve, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (flowers May-Jul in racemes; capsule ~5 mm; seeds 0.5 mm with a 3 mm hair tuft, 100,000-286,000 seeds/kg); Wikipedia (blooms July-November); USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (insect cross-pollination, many-seeded capsules). Flower life, fruit set, ripening and crop estimated.

canopy.silhouette: low wide feathery crown on crooked trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two thick oblong cotyledons, a first once-pinnate leaf, then bright green, feathery bipinnate leaves with a few pairs of long leaflets and paired spines at the nodes of a zigzag stem. The taproot races ahead and a bud zone at the stem base resprouts if the top is killed, so young plants become low, thorny, multi-stemmed bushes; suppressed plants decades old can look like seedlings.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Prosopis glandulosa (scarified seed germinates in ~7 h at 33 C; best emergence from 0.5-1.5 cm; seed by age 3; 27-yr-old plants 0.2-1.5 m in an exclosure; trees 6-12 m; max ages 110-217 yr, most under 100); ICRAF Agroforestree (3-9 m; first fruit at 3-4 yr).

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS P. glandulosa (spring racemes with the leaves; bee pollinated, 160+ bee species; pods 10-20 cm, ~12 seeds, mature in 2-3 months, fall by late summer; 97-131 pods/tree in one study); ICRAF (racemes 5-14 cm; pods 8-30 cm, straw-yellow or violet-tinged). Flowers per raceme, fruit set and decay estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 long, narrow, fleshy cotyledons and a coiled embryo that uncoils fast; first leaves bright green, fleshy and cylindrical (1-4 cm) like the adult's. Grows slowly into a stiff, rigid, much-branched spiny shrub with pale bark; after 12 years only about 0.7 m tall on dry sites. Resprouts from the root crown.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Sarcobatus vermiculatus (transplants 0.73 m tall after 12 yr; to 3 m; vigorous crown sprouting); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (67-91% germination in 2-10 days at 10 C); lifespan estimated from its slow growth

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS and Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (monoecious, wind-pollinated; male flowers in small cone-like spikes at twig tips, female flowers single in leaf axils; tan winged utricles 4-5 mm, 1 cm across the wing, mature late Sep-Nov, a few hang until next summer)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two small fleshy cotyledons, then succulent, jointed, bead-like green stems with only tiny scale leaves, like a miniature pickleweed. It branches from the base into a low, knobbly bush of upright jointed green stems whose segments are often nearly round; the lower stems turn woody and grey, and the plant traps blown sand and salt crust into a hummock.
growth.source: Wikipedia (low shrub to 1.8 m of alkali flats; knobby fleshy jointed green stems with scale leaves; seeds eaten in prehistory) and Gul & Weber 1999 (Can. J. Bot.: fast germination in fresh to saline water). Growth rate, first seed and lifespan estimated from related perennial chenopod shrubs.

fruiting.source: Estimated from floras (Jepson / Intermountain Flora as recalled: tiny flowers 3-5 per fleshy bract in cylindric spikes 5-25 mm at the stem tips, summer, wind-pollinated; utricle ~1 mm; spikes break up in autumn) and Wikipedia (seeds ground for food in prehistory).

shrub.name: Mediterranean saltbush
shrub.origin: Mediterranean, N Africa and Middle East

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds, held in a pair of papery bracts, germinate within days once rain has washed some of the salt out of them. The seedling has two narrow cotyledons, then small silvery, scurfy, diamond-shaped leaves; it grows fast into a dense, much-branched, silver-grey bush with whitish stems.
growth.source: Le Houerou, The role of saltbushes (Atriplex spp.) in arid land rehabilitation (A. halimus 1-3 m, fast-growing, long-lived browse shrub of North African chotts and sebkhas); Flora of Israel; ages estimated.

shrub.source: Atriplex halimus L., Mediterranean saltbush (sea orache): silver-grey shrub 1-3 m of salty plains, chott and sebkha margins around the Mediterranean, the Sahara edge and the Middle East. Kew POWO; Le Houerou; Flora of North Africa; Flora of Israel.

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within hours on wet sand or silt left by a flood; the seedling is a minute two-leaved sprout that grows 2-5 mm a day, with a ~12 cm shoot over a longer root by 8 weeks. It becomes a dense, multi-stemmed shrub of reddish-brown stems and feathery grey-green scale-leaved twigs, pink-plumed in summer, and resprouts hard after fire or cutting.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (germination <24 h; seed viable ~24-45 days in summer; seedlings 2-5 mm/day in month 1, 11.7 cm shoot at 8 weeks; may flower in year 1, most from year 3; 4-8 m, usually <6 m; resprouts 3-4 m in one season; shrubs 75-100 yr old show no decline). Height-age curve estimated from these.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (5 sepals and petals, dense racemes of ~20 flowers per 2.5 cm on new growth; insect cross-pollinated, wind unlikely; ~22 ovules, 8-20+ tiny plumed seeds per flower; up to 2.5 x 10^8 seeds per plant per year, shed all season). Flower life, ripening and capsule persistence estimated.

ground.name: Alkali sacaton

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds need warm, wet, freshly leached soil; the seedling is a thin rolled blade that grows slowly into a tuft. Over years the bunch widens into a coarse, tough tussock up to a metre across, leaves arching outward, under wide, airy pinkish-purple panicles in summer.
growth.source: USDA FEIS and NRCS Plant Guide Sporobolus airoides (long-lived warm-season bunchgrass 0.5-1.2 m of saline and alkaline flats; seedlings slow; flowers May-Oct); ages estimated.

ground.source: Sporobolus airoides (Torr.) Torr., alkali sacaton: coarse long-lived bunchgrass 0.5-1.2 m of saline and alkaline flats and playa margins of the Great Basin and the Southwest (Bonneville basin, Death Valley margins), often with saltgrass and greasewood. Kew POWO; USDA FEIS; Flora of North America.

Flowers hide in the joints late in summer; the whole plant turns red or purple in autumn, sheds seed and dies.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rare (germination is episodic, needing fresh water on saline ground); the seedling is a small tuft of short, stiff, grey-green leaves in two neat opposite ranks. Scaly rhizomes then run through the soil and send up rows of short, stiff, leafy shoots, forming a dense, low turf patch; male and female plants are separate.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Distichlis spicata (dioecious; seeds need stratification and scarification, germination rare and episodic, seedling survival 0-95% with falling salinity; rhizomes to 180 cm long, 10-25 cm deep; 15-45 cm tall, usually <30 cm; photosynthesis rises with light). Time to flowering and clone lifespan estimated.
